samples.summary: Consolidated write path marks dirty by indexing body blocks with context-relative indices — wrong block or TypeError in header/footer
samples.evidence: `applyStyleToSelection` (new single write path for the B/I/U/S toggles, clear-formatting Cmd+\ and the format painter Cmd+Alt+V) computes `startIdx = this.doc.getBlockIndex(range.anchor.blockId)` / `endIdx = ...`. `Doc.getBlockIndex` resolves against `getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:211-213), i.e. the *header* or *footer* block array when `doc.editContext !== 'body'`. The loop then dereferences `this.doc.document.blocks[i].id` — always the BODY array. In header/footer context the indices therefore address the wrong array: the wrong block is marked dirty (stale repaint) and, when the header/footer region has more blocks than the body, `document.blocks[i]` is `undefined` and `.id` throws a TypeError, aborting the render. The keyboard toggles and clear-formatting are reachable in header/footer (the slim header/footer toolbar exists in docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:387). Note this indexing pattern pre-dates the change (it was duplicated in the old `clearFormatting`/`toggleStyle` tails), but the change makes it the single shared path and did not fix it while explicitly reworking the surrounding dirty-marking (the `getCellInfo(anchor) ?? getCellInfo(focus)` fallback right above).

samples.summary: An endpoint inside a nested table makes the whole range a silent no-op, including the reachable non-nested part
samples.evidence: `if (anchorIdx < 0 || focusIdx < 0) return;` bails out of the entire traversal when either normalized endpoint is not a context block (endpoint inside a *nested* table, or a parentage entry stale since the last layout). This converts the previous crash into a total no-op for the range: a selection running from inside a nested table down through several ordinary body paragraphs now styles *nothing at all*, not even the body paragraphs it fully covers, and the user gets no feedback (Cmd+B appears dead). `visitStyledRunsInRange` shares the same guard, so the summary also reports `{}` and the toolbar renders unpressed. The added test at packages/docs/test/model/table.test.ts:343 pins exactly this 'nothing was written' behaviour, so it is deliberate — but a partial walk (skipping only the unresolvable endpoint's block) would preserve the read/write symmetry the module argues for without dropping the reachable paragraphs.

samples.summary: Toolbar render path now performs a full selection traversal on every re-render (and again per toggle click)
samples.evidence: `const styleSummary = editor?.getRangeStyleSummary();` runs on every render of `TextFormatGroup`, and each of `toggleBold`/`toggleItalic`/`toggleUnderline`/`toggleStrike` calls `editor.getRangeStyleSummary()` again on click. In the docs editor that call now goes through `visitStyledRunsInRange` (editor.ts:2720), which walks every run of the selection — for a select-all, every block of the document; for a cross-block selection containing a table, every block of every cell (range-slices.ts:168-177). The four toggles previously read the O(1) caret style. Toolbars re-render on every cursor move / keystroke via `onCursorMove`, so this is a per-keystroke O(document) walk on large selections. Same pattern in mobile-toolbar.tsx:229 and docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:393-405 (which calls the summary once more per toggle). Correctness is unaffected; responsiveness on large documents may be.

finding.summary: Consolidated write path marks dirty by indexing body blocks with context-relative indices — wrong block or TypeError in header/footer
finding.evidence: `applyStyleToSelection` (new single write path for the B/I/U/S toggles, clear-formatting Cmd+\ and the format painter Cmd+Alt+V) computes `startIdx = this.doc.getBlockIndex(range.anchor.blockId)` / `endIdx = ...`. `Doc.getBlockIndex` resolves against `getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:211-213), i.e. the *header* or *footer* block array when `doc.editContext !== 'body'`. The loop then dereferences `this.doc.document.blocks[i].id` — always the BODY array. In header/footer context the indices therefore address the wrong array: the wrong block is marked dirty (stale repaint) and, when the header/footer region has more blocks than the body, `document.blocks[i]` is `undefined` and `.id` throws a TypeError, aborting the render. Note this indexing pattern pre-dates the change (it was duplicated in the old `clearFormatting`/`toggleStyle` tails), but the change makes it the single shared path and did not fix it while explicitly reworking the surrounding dirty-marking (the `getCellInfo(anchor) ?? getCellInfo(focus)` fallback right above).

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. text-editor.ts:2935-2936 derives block indices via this.doc.getBlockIndex(), which resolves against getContextBlocks() (document.ts:211-213, 98-101 → header/footer arrays when editContext !== 'body'), while the dirty loop at 2950-2952 dereferences this.doc.document.blocks[i].id, always the body array (document.ts:76-78). The only guard is startIdx/endIdx < 0 (2937), which does not fire for a valid header index that is out of range for the body array — so document.blocks[i] can be undefined and .id throws a TypeError, aborting the render; in the non-throwing case the wrong (body) block is marked dirty, leaving the edited header/footer block stale. The path is reachable in header/footer: setEditContext (247-252) sets doc.editContext, and toggleStyle (874-904), clearFormatting (928) and the format-painter apply (1008-1012) all run through handleKeyDown (696) with no header/footer bail-out; header/footer caret+selection editing is a supported flow (test/view/hf-caret-selection.test.ts). This is a runtime crash / incorrect state-update bug squarely in the correctness lane.
